desc:
A cluster has servers numbered 0..n-1; servers[i] is the weight of server i. There are m tasks. Task j arrives at second j and needs tasks[j] seconds to run. Arriving tasks wait in a queue in the order of their index.

At every second, while the queue is not empty and at least one server is free, the task at the front of the queue is given to the free server with the smallest weight, ties broken by the smallest index. A server that starts a task at second s is busy until second s + tasks[j], and at that very second it is free again and can accept a task.

Return an array ans of length m where ans[j] is the index of the server that runs task j.

servers = [3, 3, 2], tasks = [1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 2]
result  = [2, 2, 0, 2, 1, 2]
second 0: task 0 -> server 2 (weight 2), busy until 1
second 1: task 1 -> server 2 again, busy until 3
second 2: task 2 -> server 0 (weights tie, smaller index), busy until 5
second 3: task 3 -> server 2, busy until 5
second 4: task 4 -> server 1, busy until 5
second 5: task 5 -> server 2
hints: Simulating every second is too slow when tasks last 100,000 seconds. Which moments actually matter?
Only moments when a task is assigned matter. Keep a min-heap of free servers ordered by (weight, index) and a min-heap of busy servers ordered by finishing time.

For task j, set the current time to max(time, j). Move every busy server that finished by then back to the free heap. If no server is free, jump the time to the earliest finishing time and release again.
editorial: Use two heaps. The free heap holds (weight, index), the busy heap holds (finish time, weight, index). Keep a variable t for the time at which the current task gets assigned; because the queue is first-in-first-out, assignment times never go backwards.

For task j: first t = max(t, j), since the task cannot start before it arrives. Release from the busy heap all servers with finish time ≤ t. If the free heap is still empty, the task has to wait: set t to the smallest finish time and release again (this may free several servers at once, and the tie-break among them is exactly the heap order). Then pop the best free server, record it, and push it to the busy heap with finish time t + tasks[j].
Each task causes a constant number of heap operations, so the time is O((n + m) log n) and the memory O(n).
solution:
import heapq


def assignTasks(servers, tasks):
    free = [(w, i) for i, w in enumerate(servers)]
    heapq.heapify(free)
    busy = []
    ans = []
    t = 0
    for j, d in enumerate(tasks):
        t = max(t, j)
        while busy and busy[0][0] <= t:
            _e, w, i = heapq.heappop(busy)
            heapq.heappush(free, (w, i))
        if not free:
            t = busy[0][0]
            while busy and busy[0][0] <= t:
                _e, w, i = heapq.heappop(busy)
                heapq.heappush(free, (w, i))
        w, i = heapq.heappop(free)
        ans.append(i)
        heapq.heappush(busy, (t + d, w, i))
    return ans
